question: Why does target-aware DIN add little ranking benefit over simple pooling on exposures without a past category match, and could better target/history field interaction recover incremental signal within the frozen causal inputs? On the supplied single-seed validation receipts, DIN versus pooling improves overall AUC by 0.00313587 and category-match-present AUC by 0.00267439, but category-match-absent AUC by only 0.00026174 (717129 exposures, 29616 positives, 687513 negatives; 22.17% of validation). Logloss on the absent slice still improves from 0.17224699 to 0.17209051. These are exploratory within-slice contrasts, not evidence that absent-match examples are intrinsically harder or that query construction is the cause. Retrieve evidence to distinguish a query/interaction bottleneck from insufficient predictive history, truncated histories, field missingness, behavior composition, calibration, and seed variation before choosing a mechanism-distinct candidate.
